messages:
amelia: Heads-up: perf spike on prod after the driver roll last night. 95th latency for seq=512 generation up ~30% on the H100 fleet. Profiling attached later.

devon: :eyes: saw a similar bump in canaries?

amelia: Canaries saw a smaller increase (~10%) but prod is bigger. My quick trace shows the autotuner is picking a different kernel for the 512/2048 code paths. Snippet from selection log:
```
kernel_pick: attn-opt-512 -> attn-gen-vec-v2
expected_latency_ms: 8.2 -> observed_latency_ms: 10.6
```

sanjay: My initial hunch: the new CUDA driver changed some heuristics in cuBLAS/cudaLaunch that our kernel scoring assumes. Autotuner ranking now mis-orders kernels for certain seq/batch combos.

maria: Confirmed with nightly regression runs: after driver bump 530.x -> 534.x we see a shift in kernel score distribution. The sequence-length bias that used to pick "attn-opt-512" is preferring the generic vectorized kernel.

liam: Can we force the selector to prefer the old kernel while we root cause? We have an override hook for arch+seq.

devon: Yes. We can set REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attn-opt-512 on the H100-80gb pool. Short-term rollback plan: disable autotune and pin kernels to the pre-roll snapshot.

amelia: Also seeing increased KV-cache churn / misses when hitting the new kernel path. Memory behavior changed.

sanjay: New kernel's internal kvcache layout uses a different stride; our prefetch heuristic is now misaligned -> lower kvcache_hit_ratio. We'll add per-seq kvcache metrics.

maria: Microbenchmarks on devbox: with the driver delta throughput drops ~18% at seq=512 for batch_sizes >4. Batching heuristic appears to favor larger batches because the new kernel looks better at large batches in bench tools but worse for our latency SLO.

liam: Proposed plan: 
- short: pin kernel + disable autotune on affected pools (canary -> prod).
- medium: add selector-level fallback that penalizes kernel picks if latency regresses beyond threshold (use online A/B).
- long: extend autotuner features to include driver-version and driver-reported heuristics.

devon: I'll run the short fix. Steps:
1) set kernel override on canary H100 pool (5 nodes)
2) run 1k requests across our seq distribution
3) if stable, roll to prod in 10% increments
4) keep current driver but mark as investigated/unsupported until root cause known

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: rollback-kernel-override -> canary-h100 (job 4235). ETA ~3m.

amelia: Add tracing: log kernel selection rationale to traces for any pick that deviates from baseline policy. Need the raw decision reasons.

sanjay: I'll add a dashboard panel for kvcache_hit_ratio and kernel_pick_counts broken down by seq. Also set an alert: 95th latency > baseline * 1.2 over 30m.

maria: Also capture CUDA driver API version and cuBLAS library minor version in the request environment so we can correlate picks to driver details.

liam: Important: prefer kernel pin over driver rollback. Full driver rollback requires infra windows and has larger blast radius.

devon: Starting canary now and attaching profiling traces. Will post updates.

deploy-bot: deploy success: rollback-kernel-override canary -> completed. job 4235. duration 2m12s.

devon: Canary looks good: 95th back to baseline. Beginning 10% prod roll. Monitoring for 30m.

maria: Uploaded profiling tarball: s3://redwood-perf/1802503333/profiles.tar.gz (contains perf traces, CUDA API logs, kernel selection diffs).

amelia: Thanks all. Follow-up tickets: autotuner driver-feature flag, selector fallback logic, kvcache prefetch patch. I'll file JIRA and link traces.

devon: Will keep the override in place until we have an autotune patch and regression tests.

amelia: Please add notes in the postmortem if we need a driver rollback later. For now, kernel pin + improved metrics seems to stabilize.

(End of thread)
